alignments.note: Construct noun of the superscription chain; the indefinite *A* belongs to the nominal expression it determines under rule 15, since Hebrew has no indefinite article.

Article on the nomen rectum. The ASV writes no *the* anywhere in the phrase (*A Song of Ascents*), so under rule 29's closing sentence the article is unrepresented; the *A* is the construct noun's own under rule 15 and is not a fronted determiner.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's relational *of* under rule 19, headed on the noun.

Imperative with its subject pronoun. Rule 36: a *ye* written immediately after the imperative is that verb's subject pronoun, while the second *ye* (t010) stands before the vocative noun and is that noun's.
Definite direct-object marker; the ASV writes the object bare (*bless ye Jehovah*), so rule 16's default applies.
Divine name as object of the imperative.
Quantifier on the vocative phrase, rendered *all*.
Vocative noun with the supplied *ye* standing before it, which rule 36 keeps in the noun's own unit; it is never `added`. Head on the noun carrying the lexeme.
Nomen rectum of `עַבְדֵי יְהוָה`, taking the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Attributive article on the participle, rendered by a relative rather than a *the*; rule 41 gives that relative to the article and heads the unit on it.

Participle keeps its own English verb; the relative before it is the article's under rule 41. Unit discontinuous from its relative only in the sense that the ASV fronts the adverbial phrase *by night* between them (rule 25).
Construct noun; no article morpheme stands on it, so the written *the* is supplied to the construct under rule 29, the rectum's own article being absent here.
Nomen rectum taking the chain's *of* under rule 19.
Temporal preposition rendered *by* in *by night*; the phrase is fronted before the participle, so this unit and s018 stand apart from the verb under rule 25.
Article assimilated into the pointed preposition and supplied by MACULA as its own token (rule 12). The ASV writes *by night* with no *the*, so it is unrepresented.
Plural noun rendered by the English singular *night*; the ASV's number is followed as written.

review_notes: The superscription is aligned as ordinary source text: `שִׁיר` takes *A Song* with the indefinite article under rule 15, and the article on `מַעֲלוֹת` is unrepresented because the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all (rule 29).
The verse writes two supplied/written *ye*s; they are allocated by position under rule 36 — the first to the imperative, the second to the vocative `עַבְדֵי`.
`הָעֹמְדִים` is split under rule 41: the article takes the relative *That* and the participle keeps *stand*, with the fronted `בַּלֵּילוֹת` standing between them (rule 25).
